rows.jp: 「その息子ってのが、豊なんだよな」
rows.en: “The son I mentioned was Yutaka.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "That son was, of course, Yutaka."

rows.jp: 霧は反応できていなかった。
rows.en: Kiri is unable to react.

ghs.en: Kiri was unable to react.

rows.jp: 手の震えは止まっていた。
rows.en: Her hand has stopped trembling.

ghs.en: The shaking of her hands stopped.

rows.jp: 落ち着いた……わけではなかった。
rows.en: Not because she has... calmed down.

ghs.en: Calming down... was not the cause.
ghs.assessment: The stillness does not mean that Kiri has calmed down. 'Was not the cause' treats calming as a cause rather than a rejected interpretation.

highlights.text: Calming down... was not the cause.

rows.jp: 愕然とした表情で、俺を見ている。
rows.en: She stares at me, aghast.

ghs.en: Terror in her facial expression, she looks at me.
ghs.assessment: 愕然 describes a stunned or shocked expression. 'Terror' identifies fear rather than shocked disbelief.

highlights.text: Terror in her facial expression, she looks at me.

rows.jp: 矢尻が俺からそれていることも、気づいていない。
rows.en: She has not even noticed that the arrowhead has veered away from me.

ghs.en: She hadn't noticed that the tip of the bolt had strayed from me.

rows.jp: 「で、読めてたかも知れないけど、Ｓってのは新川のイニシャルでもあった」
rows.en: “And, as you may already have guessed, S also happened to be Shinkawa's initial.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "And, as you maybe have guessed, 'S' is also the initial of Shinkawa."

rows.jp: 「……な、なにを言って……？」
rows.en: “...W-what are you... saying?”

ghs.en: Kiri: "...wh-, what did you say...?"
ghs.assessment: Kiri asks what Taichi is saying now. 'What did you say?' asks for repetition of a completed utterance.

highlights.text: Kiri: "...wh-, what did you say...?"

rows.jp: 半笑い。
rows.en: A half-laugh.

ghs.en: Half smile.

rows.jp: 感情さえコントロールできていない様子。
rows.en: She cannot even control her emotions.

ghs.en: She is unable to keep even emotions under control.

rows.jp: 「あいつも子供なのにあんなこと知っちゃってさ。もうまともな人生にはならないって思ってたよ」
rows.en: “He was only a child, but he'd learned things like that. I figured there was no chance he'd grow up to have a normal life.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Guy's a child, but he's well acquainted with that stuff. I thought he'd never be able to have a proper life anymore."

rows.jp: 「末は変態かジャンキーかってさ」
rows.en: “He'd end up either a pervert or a junkie.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "He'd end up as a pervert or maybe a junkie."

rows.jp: 「嘘だっっ！！」
rows.en: “That's a lie!!”

ghs.en: Kiri: "YOU LIE!!!"

rows.jp: 金切り声。
rows.en: A shriek.

ghs.en: Piercing loud scream.

rows.en: “It's a lie! It's a lie, it's a lie, it's a lie!! Don't lie to me! Have you lost your mind!? Making up something like that...”

ghs.en: Kiri: "You lie, you lie you LIE YOU LIE!!! Don't lie to me! Did you lose your mind?! You're just spreading garbage..."

rows.jp: 「事実だよ」
rows.en: “It's the truth.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "It's the truth."

rows.jp: 「そんなことあるわけない！　豊がそんなことしていたはずがない！」
rows.en: “That can't be true! Yutaka could never have done those things!”

ghs.en: Kiri: "That simply can't be! It's simply impossible that Yutaka would ever do anything like that!"

rows.en: “It is true, and Yutaka did those things.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "That simply is. Yutaka did all that."

rows.jp: 「一番張り切ってたぞ」

ghs.en: Taichi: "And he was the most enthusiastic!"

rows.jp: 笑う。

rows.en: “Well, I suppose raping a grown woman was too much for a child. Even what a woman has down there must have been a tremendous shock to him—”

highlights.text: Her voice seems to be bursting open.

ghs.en: Kiri: "I have never heard about this anywhere! We've always lived together, and he never talked about that. Impossible... unthinkable---"

highlights.text: Kiri: "I have never heard about this anywhere! We've always lived together, and he never talked about that. Impossible... unthinkable---"

highlights.text: Kiri's lips closed tight on the spot.

rows.jp: 名探偵になった気分だ。
rows.en: I feel like a great detective.

ghs.assessment: Taichi feels like a great detective. The English says that Kiri has become one.

highlights.text: It felt she had become a detective, and a great one.

ghs.assessment: Taichi boasts that the mystery is unraveling all over or practically solving itself. The English credits Kiri with unraveling it.

ghs.en: Taichi: "And, I know why that guy's leg is injured."
ghs.assessment: Taichi knows how Yutaka injured his leg. 'Why that guy's leg is injured' asks for a present condition rather than the cause of the injury event.

highlights.text: Taichi: "And, I know why that guy's leg is injured."

ghs.en: Kiri: "...eh?"

rows.en: “Because I was there.”

rows.en: “...Then... Kurosu, you knew?”

ghs.en: Kiri: "...then... Senpai... you knew he...?"

rows.jp: 「いんにゃ？」
rows.en: “Nope.”

rows.jp: 「俺は豊が生き延びたなんて思ってなかったし……豊って名前も忘れてたよ」

ghs.en: Taichi: "...meeting him was a coincidence."

ghs.en: Taichi: "I had been put into girls' clothing so... looks like there wasn't any recognizing from him either."
ghs.assessment: Because Taichi was cross-dressed, Yutaka apparently did not recognize him either. 'There wasn't any recognizing from him' is ungrammatical and obscures the object of recognition.

highlights.text: Taichi: "I had been put into girls' clothing so... looks like there wasn't any recognizing from him either."

rows.jp: だが豊は生き残った。

rows.en: “When you think about it, it was only natural.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "There was no way that that wouldn't break our spirits, nor for me nor for Yutaka."

highlights.text: Taichi: "There was no way that that wouldn't break our spirits, nor for me nor for Yutaka."

rows.en: Well, I probably can't talk my way out of this anymore.

ghs.en: Well, seems deceptions won't work anymore.

rows.jp: 俺も、吐き出したくなった。
rows.en: I wanted to get it out, too.

ghs.en: I, too, just wanted to spit it out.

rows.jp: 「すぐに殺意がわいたわけじゃない」
rows.en: “I didn't immediately want to kill him.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "It's not like I immediately fired into some murderous rage."

rows.jp: 「過去のことだしな」
rows.en: “It was in the past, after all.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "It was just a thing of the past."

rows.jp: 「だったら……！」
rows.en: “Then...!”

ghs.en: Kiri: "But then...!"

rows.jp: 流れが逆転しはじめていた。
rows.en: The tide is beginning to turn.

ghs.en: The flow began to reverse.

rows.jp: 感情のうねりは打ち寄せた波、俺を湿らせて引き返していく。
rows.en: The surge of emotion is a wave breaking over me, wetting me before it recedes.

ghs.en: The wave of her swelling emotions had broken ashore, drenched me, and is now withdrawing.
ghs.assessment: The wave had already broken and was withdrawing. The English shifts from past perfect to present progressive within the same completed observation.

highlights.text: The wave of her swelling emotions had broken ashore, drenched me, and is now withdrawing.

rows.jp: 霧。
rows.en: Kiri.

ghs.en: Kiri...

rows.jp: アタックしてきたのは、おまえの方なんだからな。
rows.en: You were the one who came at me first.

ghs.en: She had gone on the attack because that is her way.
ghs.assessment: The speaker says that the addressee was the one who came at or attacked him first. The English assigns the attack to a third-person woman and turns the reason into her general disposition.

highlights.text: She had gone on the attack because that is her way.

rows.jp: 「苦しんでいるのなら、見逃してやろうと思った」
rows.en: “If he was suffering, I was willing to let it go.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "I thought, if he's in pain, I'll let it go."
ghs.assessment: The speaker recounts his earlier thought that he would let the matter go if the other person was suffering too. 'I'll let it go' changes that embedded past intention into a present promise.

highlights.text: Taichi: "I thought, if he's in pain, I'll let it go."

rows.jp: 「けど俺とつるんでいる時のあいつは、幸せそうだった」
rows.en: “But whenever he was with me, he looked happy.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "But when he was hanging around with me, he seemed to be happy."

rows.jp: 「あの日……わたしに質問した……幸せかって……？」
rows.en: “That day... you asked me... whether he was happy...?”

ghs.en: Kiri: "That day... you asked me... was he happy...?"
ghs.assessment: The quoted question asks the speaker whether the speaker was happy. The English instead asks whether an absent male was happy.

highlights.text: Kiri: "That day... you asked me... was he happy...?"

rows.jp: 「よく覚えてるな」
rows.en: “You have a good memory.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "You remember that, good."
ghs.assessment: 'You remember that, good' is an ungrammatical splice and does not cleanly express the approving reaction to the addressee's recollection.

highlights.text: Taichi: "You remember that, good."

rows.jp: 「そうだよ。そーいう意味だ」
rows.en: “That's right. That was what I meant.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "That's right. That was what it meant."

rows.jp: 今再び、同じ問いを投げかける。
rows.en: Now I put the same question to her again.

ghs.en: And now, once again, I throw the same question at her.

rows.jp: 「なあ霧……豊は、幸せだったのかな」
rows.en: “Kiri... do you think Yutaka was happy?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Say, Kiri, I'm wondering... was Yutaka happy?"

rows.jp: ありがちな問いかけ。
rows.en: A commonplace question.

ghs.en: An usual question to ask,
ghs.assessment: The English article is wrong: 'usual' begins with a consonant sound and requires 'a,' not 'an.'

highlights.text: An usual question to ask,

rows.jp: けど。
rows.en: But.

ghs.en: but,

rows.en: I meant the exact opposite.

ghs.en: the meaning was wholly and damnably the opposite.
ghs.assessment: The source describes the question as difficult to answer; the intensifier 'damnably' adds an unsupported profane register.

highlights.text: the meaning was wholly and damnably the opposite.

rows.jp: 「……つらい思いをしてきたんです！」
rows.en: “...He had such a hard life!”

ghs.en: Kiri: "...he was feeling bitter!"
ghs.assessment: 辛い目に遭ってきた refers to undergoing painful or harsh experiences. 'Had been feeling bitter' changes external suffering into an internal resentful attitude.

highlights.text: Kiri: "...he was feeling bitter!"

rows.jp: 「親族に邪険にされて……荒れて……」
rows.en: “His relatives treated him terribly... and he went off the rails...”

ghs.en: Kiri: "His relatives were so cruel... so rough..."
ghs.assessment: The source says the person was badly treated by relatives and consequently became wild or troubled. 'Relatives were cruel, and so rough' leaves the result without its subject and makes 'rough' appear to modify the relatives.

highlights.text: Kiri: "His relatives were so cruel... so rough..."

rows.jp: 「本当にずっとつらかった？」
rows.en: “Was every last moment really painful?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Truly, always, bitter?"
ghs.assessment: The source again refers to experiencing painful or harsh treatment. 'Feeling so bitter' substitutes resentment for suffering.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Truly, always, bitter?"

rows.jp: 「一瞬でも、幸せな時間はなかった？」
rows.en: “Wasn't there even one moment when he was happy?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "There were never times of happiness, not even one instant?"

rows.jp: 「それは……」
rows.en: “Well...”

ghs.en: Kiri: "Well..."

rows.jp: 「あっただろうが」
rows.en: “There was, wasn't there?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "I'm sure there were."

rows.jp: 霧は答えない。うつむく。
rows.en: Kiri does not answer. She bows her head.

ghs.en: Kiri doesn't answer. And hangs her head.

rows.jp: 武器も下を向いている。
rows.en: The weapon is pointing down as well.

ghs.en: The weapon points down as well.

rows.jp: 敵意も殺意も萎んだ。枯れた花。
rows.en: Hostility and murderous intent have wilted. A withered flower.

ghs.en: Hostility and murderous intent too wither. A wilted flower.

rows.jp: 細い体に、疑念という毒素が満ちる。
rows.en: The poison of doubt fills her slender body.

ghs.en: Her thin slender body fills with a toxin named doubt.

rows.jp: 「そりゃそうだろうさ。昔しでかしたことを綺麗さっぱり忘れれば、心もスッキリサッパリだ。いくらだって幸せになれるさ！」
rows.en: “Of course there was. Forget every last thing you did in the past, and your heart is clean and clear. You can be as happy as you please!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Sooo, well, yeah, that's that. All the stuff he's done long ago is all beautifully and spotlessly forgotten, and his heart is all clean and refreshed. How so very happy could he become after that!"
ghs.assessment: The source concludes that once those memories are gone, the person can become as happy as can be. 'How so very happy could he become' is an ungrammatical question and loses the stated causal conclusion.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Sooo, well, yeah, that's that. All the stuff he's done long ago is all beautifully and spotlessly forgotten, and his heart is all clean and refreshed. How so very happy could he become after that!"

rows.jp: 「だから思い出させてやった」
rows.en: “So I made him remember.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "And that is why I made him remember."
Kiri: "...stop this..."

rows.en: Kiri tries to cover her ears.

ghs.en: Kiri goes to cover her ears.

rows.jp: 「塞ぐな！」
rows.en: “Don't!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Don't cover your ears!"

rows.jp: 手は止まる。
rows.en: Her hands stop.

ghs.en: Hands stop.

rows.jp: 「よく晴れた日だったよ」
rows.en: “It was a perfectly clear day.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "It was a nice clear sunny day."

rows.en: “Just as you saw, I told him everything on the roof that day.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "As you did see, that moment we talked about everything."
ghs.assessment: The speaker says that he told the other person everything on the rooftop at that time. 'That moment we talked about everything' removes the specified location and changes a one-way disclosure into mutual conversation.

highlights.text: Taichi: "As you did see, that moment we talked about everything."

rows.en: “He asked me what he had to do to make me forgive him.”

rows.en: “It wasn't a matter of forgiving him or not. The sins he committed remain forever as they are. No one can touch them, much less alter them. I had no intention of blaming him for that, either.”

ghs.assessment: The narrator says he never intended to blame the other person for the fixed facts. 'I didn't feel like there was blame then' removes both the narrator's agency and the object of blame; the preceding 'Neither there is changing them' is also ungrammatical.

highlights.text: Taichi: "There's no forgiving nor condemning. Sins perpetrated remain like that in eternity. There's no putting your hands on them in any way. Neither there is changing them. I didn't feel like there was blame then."

rows.en: “One question... Why don't you just die right now?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Say, I got one question though... why don't you just die right this very instant?"

rows.en: “...That's what I said.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "...that was what I asked."

ghs.en: Kiri: "Aaahhh..."

rows.jp: 「そしたら……あいつ本当に自殺しちゃったんだ」
rows.en: “And then... he really did kill himself.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "And then... that guy killed himself for real."

ghs.assessment: The narrator crouches beside the seated person. 'She squats cradling her knees' assigns the movement and posture to the other person.

highlights.text: She squats cradling her knees on the spot.

ghs.assessment: A pitying smile is etched on the person's face. 'A smile engraves' incorrectly makes the smile the agent of engraving and leaves the construction incomplete.

highlights.text: A smile of pity engraves on my face.

rows.en: “Either way, there is only one truth.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "However things may go, the truth is only one:"

ghs.assessment: The narrator whispers at one ear. The English plural 'ears' changes the concrete gesture.

highlights.text: I whisper in her ears,

rows.jp: プツン、と。
rows.en: Snap.

ghs.en: Snap.

ghs.assessment: The metaphorical string snapped or broke. 'Had been cut' implies an external cutting agent and changes the event into an earlier past-perfect action.

highlights.text: And so I knew that a string inside Kiri had been cut,
